library(tidyverse)

This R Shiny application was created to explore data from the ASA's Census@School project. While the full dataset has more variables, I've selected about a half dozen that can be used to filter the data and then conduct some light EDA. More information can be found on the ASA's website (link below) and you can take your students to the site to add their own responses to the survey.

The data originates from an expansive student census profile documenting baseline metrics such as school transit times preferred extra-curricular structures, digital usage baselines, and environmental profiles. Learn more at the https://ww2.amstat.org/censusatschool/.

First I want to pull in my Census at School data from 2026:
```{r}
CensusSchool <- read.csv("data/CensusAtSchool2026.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA"))
save(CensusSchool, file = "data/censusAtSchool2026.RData")
```
Because this data is not administrative, like the datasets we used in class, where every cell had a value, we need to address the missing value issue. Regression models would handle this well by just pairwise removing observations with a missing value, but our random forests cannot handle these kinds of missing values, so I'm just going to preemtively remove them.
```{r}
CensusSchool <- CensusSchool |>
  tidyr::drop_na(
    text_messages_sent_yesterday, classgrade, gender, ageyears,
    travel_time_to_school, favorite_school_subject, home_occupants, role_model_type
  )
```
Now we will split the data into training and testing subsets
```{r}
set.seed(852006)
CensusSchool_split <- rsample::initial_split(CensusSchool, prop = .7)
	CensusSchool_train <- training(CensusSchool_split)
	CensusSchool_test <- testing(CensusSchool_split)
```
Use 5 fold cross-validation to select the best model each family of models (see below). You should set up your own grid of tuning parameters for each model (even if it is just the
number of levels to look at).
```{r}
CensusSchool_CV_folds <- vfold_cv(CensusSchool_train, 5)
```
Create models for predicting a response variable you choose. You should use at least three predictors in these models.
* You should provide a thorough explanation of what a classification or regression tree model is. Then you
should fit a classification or regression tree with varying values for at least one tuning parameter.
* You should provide a thorough explanation of what a random forest is and why we might use it (be sure
to relate this to a basic tree). You should then fit a random forest model with varying values for the mtry
parameter.
```{r}
# Outcome Vars: text_messages_sent_yesterday, doing_homework_hours
# Predictor Vars: classgrade, gender, ageyears, travel_time_to_school, favorite_school_subject, home_occupants, role_model_type

# Classification or Regression Tree
CensusSchool_rec1 <- recipe(text_messages_sent_yesterday ~ classgrade + gender + travel_time_to_school + favorite_school_subject + home_occupants + role_model_type, data = CensusSchool_train) |>
  step_naomit(all_predictors()) |>
  # don't normalize the outcome, but do the rest:
  step_normalize(all_numeric(), -all_outcomes()) |>
  # create dummys:
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

CensusSchool_rec2 <- recipe(text_messages_sent_yesterday ~ classgrade + gender + ageyears + 
    travel_time_to_school + favorite_school_subject + 
    home_occupants + role_model_type, 
  data = CensusSchool_train) |>
  # don't normalize the outcome, but do the rest:
  step_normalize(all_numeric(), -all_outcomes()) |>
  # create dummys:
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  # Create the interaction term explicitly
  step_interact(terms = ~ ageyears:travel_time_to_school)
```

```{r}
CensusSchool_mod <- linear_reg() |> 
  set_engine("lm")

CensusSchool_wkfl1 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(CensusSchool_rec1) |>
  add_model(CensusSchool_mod)
CensusSchool_wkfl2 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(CensusSchool_rec2) |>
  add_model(CensusSchool_mod)

CensusSchool_wkfl1
CensusSchool_wkfl2

CensusSchool_fit1 <- CensusSchool_wkfl1 |>
  fit_resamples(CensusSchool_CV_folds)
CensusSchool_fit2 <- CensusSchool_wkfl2 |>
  fit_resamples(CensusSchool_CV_folds)


rbind(CensusSchool_fit1 |> collect_metrics() |> filter(.metric == "rmse"),
      CensusSchool_fit2 |> collect_metrics() |> filter(.metric == "rmse")) |> 
  mutate(Model = c("Model 1","Model 2")) |>
  select(Model, mean, n, std_err)
```

```{r}
CensusSchool_final_fit <-  CensusSchool_wkfl1 |>
  last_fit(split = CensusSchool_split, metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)) 
CensusSchool_final_fit |> collect_metrics()
CensusSchool_final_fit |> extract_fit_parsnip() |> tidy()

```

#### - Specify the random forest and tuning parameters
```{r}
rf_spec <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 500) |>
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity") |>
  set_mode("regression")

rf_wkf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(CensusSchool_rec1) |>
  add_model(rf_spec)
```
#### - Tune using the training-set cross-validation folds
```{r}
set.seed(9261979)
rf_fit <- rf_wkf |>
  tune_grid(resamples = CensusSchool_CV_folds, 
            grid = 10,
            metrics = metric_set(rmse))

rf_fit |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |> 
  arrange(mean)
```
#### - Select the best random forest and finalize the workflow
```{r}
rf_best_params <- select_best(rf_fit, metric = "rmse")
rf_best_params

rf_final_wkf <- rf_wkf |>
  finalize_workflow(rf_best_params)

rf_final_fit <- rf_final_wkf |>
  last_fit(CensusSchool_split, metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))
rf_final_model <- extract_workflow(rf_final_fit)
```
